name: Knowledgeable Connector
description: Ingestion + retrieval MCP connector for aw-knowledgeable (fredericowu/aw-knowledgeable), the standalone Neo4j knowledge-graph service — 7 tools mapped onto its API: upload_document, create_node, create_link, get_graph, list_documents, search_nodes (lexical name matching, for the link picker), search_graph (lexical/semantic/tree retrieval with the §12 knobs — beam_width, min_score, related_vias, bucket). This app is a thin HTTP client; it has no Neo4j driver and no knowledge of aw-knowledgeable's own tenant-isolation seam. Per docs/design/aw-knowledgeable-infra.md §10 (decision D2): the tenant a call lands in comes from THIS app's own shared service secret, never from the calling agent's self-asserted headers.

skills.description: How to use the 13 MCP tools this app exposes for fredericowu/aw-knowledgeable — knowledge_search and the lower-level graph/retrieval tools, the fs-sync pending-deletion queue, and the execution-history projection.

tasks.name: KB bulk-ingest — tick
tasks.prompt: The `KB bulk-ingest — tick` task (docs/design/aw-knowledgeable-v2-retrieval.md §13, git backend §16) just exited non-zero. Run `aw-workspace-cli knowledgeable-ingest status` and read the command's own stderr above to tell which case this is: (1) the §13.5.2 ignition guard blocked it because entity extraction is claiming — expected and fine, do not re-enable or disable anything, just note it; (1b) the §6 workspace_slug refusal — AW_WORKSPACE is unset, a real config gap (this driver uploads by path since card 3fa5bf3b, so the slug is part of the document identity and is never defaulted), open a blocker; (2) a real HTTP/transport failure reaching aw-knowledgeable; (3) a batch of upload failures piling up in the journal; (4) git_state: no_secret — the git_token hasn't been set yet, expected until Frederico creates the PAT, just note it; (5) git_state: auth_failed — the PAT is missing/revoked/wrong, open a blocker so it gets rotated; (6) git_state: diverged — the mirror repo was edited outside this connector (or handed over non-empty) — NEVER force-push or merge to clear this, just report it and let a human resolve it on GitHub; (7) git_state: push_failed — report the detail, likely transient/network. Report which one, and only open a blocker if it's (2), (3), (5), or an ongoing (7) — not a single transient blip. Never run `aw-workspace-cli restart core` or touch `EXTRACTION_ENABLED`.

tasks.name: KB fs-sync — tick
tasks.prompt: The `KB fs-sync — tick` task (docs/design/aw-knowledgeable-fs-sync.md §3/§7/§20/§21) just exited non-zero. Run `aw-workspace-cli knowledgeable-sync status` and read the command's own stderr above to tell which case this is: (1) the §6 workspace_slug refusal — AW_WORKSPACE is unset, a real config gap, open a blocker; (2) another fs-sync tick already in progress — expected under overlap, just note it; (3) the §7 mass-delete valve tripped — check `status` for `valve_tripped` and the tree before approving anything in the UI, this is the one that protects the corpus, do not clear it yourself. A §20 per-prefix quiet period holding uploads (`holding` in `status`) is NOT a failure and never produces a non-zero exit on its own. A latched valve (3) also suspends §21's unattended deletion approval — surfaced as `auto_approve_suspended` in the tick result — until an audited `POST /fs-sync/valve/clear`; do not clear it yourself. Report which case, and only open a blocker for (1) or an unexplained (3).

tasks.name: KB exec-history sync — tick
tasks.prompt: The `KB exec-history sync — tick` task (docs/design/execution-history-in-production-neo4j.md §4/§8) just exited non-zero. Run `aw-workspace-cli knowledgeable-exec-sync status` and read the command's own stderr above to tell which case this is: (1) `exec_sync_enabled is false` — expected while the feature is off, just note it, do NOT turn the flag on yourself; (2) `apmt_database_url is not set` or `exec_sync_source_tenant is not set` — a real config gap, open a blocker (never guess either value: a wrong tenant reads zero rows and reports a clean tick); (3) `no service secret saved` — the connector's X-Internal-Secret is missing, open a blocker; (4) `another exec-sync tick is already in progress` — expected under overlap with a manual run, just note it; (5) `cannot read the sync sentinel` — aw-knowledgeable is unreachable or the exec routes are not deployed yet, report it; (6) `partial: ingest batch N failed` — the watermark only advanced over the prefix that landed, so the next tick resumes at the gap; one blip is fine, a repeating one is a blocker. NEVER point this at the production Neo4j directly and never run `scripts/load_exec_retrieval_neo4j.py` against it — that script wipes its target. Do not enable anything that spends on an LLM provider.

tasks.name: KB exec-history — weekly reconcile
tasks.prompt: The `KB exec-history — weekly reconcile` task (docs/design/execution-history-in-production-neo4j.md §8) reported a count mismatch between AP-MT Postgres and the exec projection in Neo4j. Read the printed table before concluding drift — the rows fail for different reasons: a `CHILD_OF`/`QA_OF` mismatch is frequently CORRECT behaviour (an endpoint outside the loaded window creates no edge by design, which is why those two rows are counted as SQL joins rather than column-not-null counts), whereas a missing `ExecRun`/`ExecToolCall` count is an ingest batch that failed and should show up in the sync tick's own history too. Postgres is the system of record: the supported repair is forward — wipe and re-backfill the projection (`POST /api/exec/wipe` then let the sync catch up), never editing the graph by hand and never editing Postgres. Report which rows drifted and by how much; open a blocker only if the drift is in a node/ToolCall count and is growing.

base_url.title: aw-knowledgeable base URL
base_url.description: Reached by container NAME on aw-stack-net, never an IP (docs/design/aw-knowledgeable-infra.md §10, D2 Q2). aw-host sits on aw-stack's own Docker network, so this resolves from inside aw-app-mcp-gateway as long as the aw-knowledgeable compose service declares an explicit container_name/alias matching this host.

service_secret.title: Service secret
service_secret.description: The X-Internal-Secret this connector authenticates every call with. Must equal aw-knowledgeable's own KNOWLEDGEABLE_SERVICE_SECRET, which that service maps 1:1 to one KNOWLEDGEABLE_SERVICE_TENANT_ID — never a caller-supplied header (D2 §Q3). Stored in the workspace secret store, read fresh on every tool call so a rotated secret needs no restart.

git_remote_url.title: Git backend — remote URL
git_remote_url.description: docs/design/aw-knowledgeable-fs-sync.md §16. An HTTPS repo URL (e.g. https://github.com/fredericowu/knowledge-base-private.git) that each sync tick commits and pushes knowledge_base/ to. A userinfo-bearing URL (https://user:token@...) is rejected — put the credential in the Git token field below instead. Empty disables the git backend entirely: no git_state is ever recorded.

git_branch.title: Git backend — branch
git_branch.description: The branch this connector pushes to, fast-forward-only. A non-fast-forward rejection (someone edited the mirror on GitHub, or the remote was handed over non-empty) is surfaced as git_state: diverged and never force-pushed.

git_token.title: Git backend — token
git_token.description: A fine-grained GitHub PAT scoped to the one repo above, Contents read/write only. Stored in the workspace secret store (never in git_remote_url, never on disk, never in argv), injected per git invocation as an environment-only Authorization header. Read fresh every tick — rotation needs no restart.

auth_required.title: Require workspace identity on every route
auth_required.description: Must be set to false for GET /keys/{slot} (docs/design/knowledgeable-apmt-key-pull-through.md) to answer production aw-knowledgeable, which holds no workspace session or API key — only the shared X-Internal-Secret. This flag is app-wide, not per-route, so every OTHER route in routes.py carries its own explicit _require_identity dependency to stay protected once this is false; do not add a new route here without the same guard.

sync_quiet_rules.title: Sync quiet periods
sync_quiet_rules.description: docs/design/aw-knowledgeable-fs-sync.md §20. Comma- or newline-separated rules `prefix=quiet_seconds[:max_hold_seconds]`. A changed file under `prefix` uploads only once its content has been unchanged for quiet_seconds; max_hold (default 4× quiet, 0 = unlimited) syncs it anyway if it has been continuously changing that long. Longest matching prefix wins. Paths matching no rule keep the built-in 30s debounce. A malformed entry is skipped and surfaced as quiet_rules_invalid in GET /fs-sync/status rather than silently disabling the feature.

delete_policy.title: Unattended deletion approval
delete_policy.description: docs/design/aw-knowledgeable-fs-sync.md §21. Comma- or newline-separated rules `prefix=auto[:min_missing_scans]` or `prefix=manual`. Longest matching prefix wins; paths matching no rule stay `manual` (today's behaviour — a human approves in the Library UI). `min_missing_scans` defaults to 2, the same tick a delete mark lands. An empty prefix is rejected (no blanket auto-approve, ever) and so is an `auto` rule anchored at `authored/` (§4's downsync is not yet exercised) — both are skipped and surfaced as delete_policy_invalid in GET /fs-sync/status rather than silently disabling or silently enabling anything. Default empty ships inert, byte-identical to today. Auto-approval also stays off whenever the §7 mass-delete valve is latched, until an audited POST /fs-sync/valve/clear.

exec_sync_enabled.title: Execution-history sync — enabled
exec_sync_enabled.description: docs/design/execution-history-in-production-neo4j.md §9 step 2. Ships FALSE: step 1 (aw-knowledgeable's schema, templates and K7 test) is deployable on its own, and turning this on is a separate operator decision. With this off the tick is a no-op and nothing is written to the production graph. Turning it on starts a 10-minute incremental MERGE-upsert of AP-MT run metadata and SCRUBBED run/tool-call text into an Exec*-labelled subgraph in the reserved, unregistered `_exec-history` bucket — structurally disjoint from the knowledge corpus (no shared labels, zero edges between them) and reachable only by the service caller. Postgres stays the system of record; rollback is POST /api/exec/wipe, one batched label-scoped delete.

exec_sync_source_tenant.title: Execution-history sync — AP-MT source tenant
exec_sync_source_tenant.description: The agents-platform-multitenant `tenant_id` to READ runs from. Deliberately not defaulted (§12 risk 7): AP-MT's tenant namespace and aw-knowledgeable's graph `tenant` namespace are different things that happen to be 1:1 today, the write-side tenant is whatever this connector's service secret resolves to server-side, and a wrong value here reads zero rows and reports a clean tick. The tick refuses to run while this is empty rather than guessing `tenant-bootstrap`. Recorded on the sync sentinel so a mis-mapped sync is visible instead of silent.

apmt_database_url.title: Execution-history sync — AP-MT Postgres DSN
apmt_database_url.description: The Postgres DSN the exec sync reads AP-MT runs from, e.g. postgresql://postgres:…@aw-remote-host-postgres:5432/agents_platform_multitenant (reachable BY NAME; 127.0.0.1 is refused from app containers). Stored in the workspace secret store like `service_secret`, never in plain app config — a DSN carries a password. This connector holds the Postgres credential and the service secret, and deliberately NEVER holds the Neo4j password: scrubbing and loading are connector-side for exactly that reason (§4), and this side never speaks Bolt.
apmt_database_url.x-reason: read-only access to AP-MT runs for the execution-history projection

source_callback_url.title: Knowledge Sources — callback URL
source_callback_url.description: docs/design/knowledgeable-knowledge-sources-registry.md §4b. The base URL aw-knowledgeable POSTs back to for this workspace's `POST /source-query` fan-out leg (e.g. this connector's own public edge URL). Pushed on every sources_sync tick alongside the forward_upstreams inventory — empty is not a configuration error: the sync still runs, and the workspace's row lands `reachable=false, reason="no callback_url configured"` on the server, visibly rather than silently.

forward_upstreams.title: Forwardable upstreams
forward_upstreams.description: docs/design/knowledgeable-connector-tool-forwarder.md + docs/design/knowledgeable-forwarder-declared-mcp-transport.md. Each entry is {id, transport, app_slug, tools (tool allow-list, each with a per-tool argument allow-list), probe {tool, ttl_ok_s, ttl_fail_s, timeout_s}, timeout_s, query_tool}. `transport` selects how the app's MCP surface is reached, and is the only field that changes the destination. Two kinds: `app-mcp` reaches `http://127.0.0.1:$AW_PORT/api/apps/<app_slug>/mcp` with `X-Api-Key=$AW_WORKSPACE_API_KEY`, under this connector's own authorization and never the caller's — only a Tier-1 app with `routes:register` can have that route. `app-mcp-json` adds a `server` field and resolves the URL, headers and enabled-state, fresh per call, from the installed app's rendered `apps/<app_slug>/mcp.json` (the file src/apps/mcp_template.py generates and aw-mcp-gateway's app-scan already trusts) — the transport a Tier-2 container app needs, since it runs no workspace-side code and so has no loopback route at all. An entry can never carry a URL or a header of its own, and `app-mcp-json` sends ONLY the headers the app declared: `AW_WORKSPACE_API_KEY` travels to 127.0.0.1 only, never to a declared endpoint. An unknown `transport` value is reported by name and never falls back to loopback. An unlisted tool or argument is rejected by name at the boundary, never silently dropped — `projectPath` is deliberately absent from codegraph's own arg allow-list below, since it would otherwise be a filesystem-read primitive over repos/**, and `filter`/`selectFields`/raw `start`/`end` are absent from signoz's for the same reason. `query_tool` ({tool, arg}, optional — docs/design/knowledgeable-knowledge-sources-registry.md §4b) names which allow-listed tool and argument `POST /source-query` uses to answer a generic natural-language query for this upstream; absent entries fall back to the codegraph default. Ships with codegraph (app-mcp) and signoz (app-mcp-json) as defaults so both paths are exercised, not dormant. Since docs/design/knowledgeable-nl-tool-adapter.md §2 each entry also carries a **capability declaration**: `accepts_natural_language` (bool, ABSENT or truthy = today's path byte-identically, only an explicit `false` activates the NL→tool-calling adapter — that one rule is the whole migration story, no existing entry on any workspace changes behaviour), `problem_domain` (what kind of question this source answers, declared for BOTH kinds — documentation today, the field a source planner would route on tomorrow), `query_guidance` (NL-false only: how this source's tools must actually be driven) and `adapter` ({max_rounds default 6, budget_s default 90}, optional). Per-tool `hint` text lives INSIDE the existing `tools.<name>` object, beside that tool's own `args` allow-list, so the allow-list and its semantics cannot drift apart. Hints are prompt text, not JSON Schema — argument names still come from `args`, and the forwarder still rejects an unlisted tool or argument by name. `query_tool` stays meaningful only for NL-true sources; an NL-false entry keeps it harmlessly so a Connector that predates the flag keeps behaving exactly as today (§6). `accepts_natural_language`/`problem_domain` sync up to aw-knowledgeable; `query_guidance` and the per-tool hints deliberately never leave the workspace where the adapter loop runs.

default.problem_domain: code structure and call graphs of this workspace's repos: where a symbol is defined, what calls it, which files implement a flow, how far a change's blast radius spreads across repos.

signoz_list_services.hint: service inventory in the window; cheap first call when the service is unknown

signoz_search_logs.hint: searchText = literal CONTAINS, NOT semantic; prefer severity+service+timeRange and omit searchText unless matching an exact token

signoz_get_field_keys.hint: which log/trace attributes exist; call before filtering on workspace-specific fields

signoz_get_field_values.hint: real values of one attribute, e.g. actual service names

default.problem_domain: observability for this workspace's own services: application logs, traces, service inventory (SigNoz). Ask it about runtime errors, exceptions, latency, what services exist and how they behave in a time window.
default.query_guidance: You cannot send natural language to any tool here. searchText is literal CONTAINS over raw log text — use it only for exact tokens you expect verbatim in a log line (an error class, an id), never for a restated question. Start broad: severity + timeRange (+ service when known), then narrow. Discover real attribute values with signoz_get_field_values before filtering on anything workspace-specific. Time ranges like '1h'/'24h'/'7d'.

apps.reason: This app contributes an mcp.json entry (the 'knowledgeable' server) that MCP Gateway discovers and merges; without the gateway no agent can reach its tools.

dependencies.note: Runtime-enforced app dependency: aw-workspace loads mcp-gateway before this app so the gateway can scan knowledgeable/mcp.json.
